clue.text: As old as Iago, for example

definitions.meaning: aged, belonging to the distant past
in Othello, Iago holds the rank of ..., an old word for an ensign or standard-bearer

explanation.definitionFit: The word means very old, and is also the archaic military rank of ensign that Shakespeare gives Iago.

clue.text: It may signify captain of a jolly group

parts.note: a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
a band is a group of people or musicians

explanation.surface: A man leads a cheerful gang of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective but is the old naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A team captain wears a band on the sleeve as a mark of office.

clue.text: Tales of the river-bank providing little or no interest?

definitions.text: Tales of the river-bank providing little or no interest?

parts.words: Tales of the river-bank providing little or no interest?
parts.note: stories of a flowing stream would be reports of its flow, and these bank products famously pay little or no interest to the holder

explanation.surface: Dull stories about life by the river bore the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyday bank holdings for paying in and drawing out typically earn little or nothing in interest.

clue.text: Put out? Give date of retirement

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the word is read in the backwards direction

parts.note: a date is a point in time, so time stands for date

explanation.surface: Someone sacked is told the day their working life ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of retirement' turns TIME round to give the answer; 'Give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, a synonym of putting out light or smoke.

clue.text: Giant said to squeeze

indicators.note: said tells us the word for giant is spoken, giving a different spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: a titan is a giant, from the giant gods of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A huge figure is reported to crush something.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten a grip is to squeeze harder, a close synonym.

clue.text: Way of producing beer in the shorter dictionary

indicators.note: in places the beer inside the shortened dictionary

parts.note: the dictionary made shorter is the common abbreviation dict
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A brewing method is described in a concise reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the shorter dictionary' suggests the Shorter Oxford, but it means the word cut down to DICT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional manner of speaking, the way words are produced in an area.

clue.text: Lament for deranged old peer

indicators.note: deranged means disordered, so the letters of these two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A mournful song for an elderly aristocrat who has lost his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplore is to regret or bewail, a synonym of lament.

clue.text: Air of artist crowned with gold

indicators.note: in a down entry being crowned means having the gold placed on top

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter wears a golden crown and looks the part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crowned with' puts AU above RA in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is the distinctive atmosphere or air surrounding a person.

clue.text: Resolute sewing method, say, of American novelist

indicators.note: say tells us these words are only spoken alike, not spelt the same

parts.note: resolute means earnest, and a sewing method could be a hemming way, a way of turning up a hem

explanation.surface: A determined approach to needlework belongs to a US writer.
explanation.walkthrough: EARNEST HEMMING WAY, said aloud, gives the name of the author of The Old Man and the Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Nobel-winning US writer of The Old Man and the Sea.

clue.text: Anguish of fellows in the wrong?

indicators.note: in places the fellows inside the legal wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Men who have done wrong suffer for it.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT, a civil wrong in legal language, surrounds MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe suffering, a synonym of anguish.

clue.text: Husband of Margaret A. Perrin in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests something in a mess, so the letters of the name are put in disarray

explanation.surface: A woman's spouse is having difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband is a spouse, the male partner in a wedded couple.

clue.text: State claim

explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert firmly, so it matches both declaring and asserting.

clue.text: A wild shot from a musketeer

indicators.note: a wild shot misses its mark, so the letters of shot are scattered

explanation.surface: A soldier with a musket fires off a stray round.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of Dumas's three musketeers, with Porthos and Aramis.

clue.text: Caribbean youth, say, mislead internally

indicators.note: internally means inside, so the answer is taken from within the word mislead

explanation.surface: A young West Indian, perhaps, gives false directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'youth' seems to be a young person, but the Isle of Youth is an island off Cuba.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isla de la Juventud, or Isle of Youth, is a Cuban island, an example of a land mass in the sea.

clue.text: Loony British host

parts.note: a host is an army, as in the heavenly host

explanation.surface: A crazy person from Britain is hosting a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' looks like a party-giver but is an old word for an army.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmy is British slang for mad, a synonym of loony.

clue.text: Focal point of four in grass

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the slang word for the drug

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, also called grass
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people sit centre stage on a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is not a lawn but cannabis, POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot is the central point on which something turns.

clue.text: Stop is about right to discharge rail passengers

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for stop goes round the letter for right

parts.note: to detain is to stop or hold back

explanation.surface: A halt is just right for letting people off a train.
explanation.definitionFit: To detrain is to let people get off a train, the railway counterpart of disembarking.

clue.text: Neat description of the pie mixed with last of suet

indicators.note: a pie filling is mixed, so the letters of these words are stirred into a new order
last of tells us to take only the final letter of suet

explanation.surface: A tidy account of making a pastry with suet stirred in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' makes EPITHE from THE PIE; 'last of' adds the T of suet.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is an apt descriptive word or phrase, often a neatly chosen label.

clue.text: Medical disorder that may recur?

indicators.note: a disorder is a lack of order, so the letters of the word medical are jumbled

explanation.surface: An illness that might come back.
explanation.walkthrough: A recurring decimal repeats its digits forever, so 'recur' fits the number not an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Some fractions written out in base ten have digits that repeat endlessly.

clue.text: Bother about right sort of dumper?

annotationWithheld.why: Bother about right sort of dumper? (7): DITHER (bother) needs C inserted, but 'about' would have to be both C and the insertion indicator, and 'right' gives no letters.
annotationWithheld.clue: Bother about right sort of dumper?

clue.text: Clearly and lazily after endless good fortune

indicators.note: after places the word for lazily following the shortened word for fortune
endless means without its final letter, so the word for fortune is cut short

parts.note: luck is good fortune
idly means lazily

explanation.surface: Someone thinks plainly and idly following a stroke of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the K off LUCK, and 'after' puts IDLY behind LUC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucidly means in a plain, easily understood manner, a synonym of clearly.

clue.text: One badly treated on the way in

definitions.meaning: a person who is walked over by others
a mat placed at the entrance to a house

explanation.definitionFit: It is a mat at the front entrance, and figuratively a person others walk all over.

clue.text: Cast down drain

definitions.meaning: to sap the spirits or press downwards

explanation.definitionFit: To depress is to dispirit someone, sapping their energy, and to press something downwards.

clue.text: Strange, dear pet is thinner at one end

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so these letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd beloved animal has a thin tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapered describes something narrowing gradually towards a point.

clue.text: Reversible pipe

indicators.note: reversible says the word reads the same either way round

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.definitionFit: To toot is to sound a horn or pipe, and to pipe is to play a whistle.

clue.text: Compass to catch in one quarter

indicators.note: in places the slang for catch inside the compass quarter

parts.note: SE, south-east, is one quarter of the compass
to cop is slang for to catch

explanation.surface: A navigational instrument helps to trap something in one area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compass' looks like the instrument, but means range.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope and compass both mean the range or extent of something.

clue.text: Overturned vessels break

indicators.note: overturned means upside down, so the word for vessels is read backwards

parts.note: pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: Upturned boats are broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to break suddenly, a close synonym.

clue.text: Pen-rack?

definitions.meaning: an enclosure or stall for animals
a manger or rack holding fodder

explanation.definitionFit: A crib is both an animal stall and a manger or hay rack in which fodder is placed.

clue.text: Dead spirit to rap

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A ghost knocks on the walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests a ghost but is the drink RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum is to tap or beat repeatedly, a synonym of rap.

clue.text: Fight of the century?

parts.note: a big boxing match is often billed this way, but here it is a conflict that literally lasted a hundred years or so

explanation.surface: A boxing promoter's hype for a big bout.
explanation.definitionFit: This conflict between England and France ran from 1337 to 1453, well over a century.

clue.text: Oleander grew with laurel

parts.note: rose means grew or increased
bay is the laurel tree

explanation.surface: A flowering shrub grew alongside a laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosebay is another name for the oleander, a flowering shrub.

clue.text: Language someday to be translated

indicators.note: translated means converted, so these letters are converted into a new order

explanation.surface: A tongue that will one day be rendered into another.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoyed is a group of Uralic languages of northern Siberia.
